newsitem.title: POLAND: POLIFARB CN DOUBLES ISSUE FOR MERGER.
newsitem.headline: POLIFARB CN DOUBLES ISSUE FOR MERGER.

text.p: Shareholders of Polish paint maker Polifarb Cieszyn voted to double to six million shares a bonus issue to facilitate a merger with Polifarb Wroclaw and give Cieszyn shareholders 53.5 percent of the new firm.

The extraordinary shareholders meeting supported a proposal by First Polish Mutual Fund Company Pioneer to increase the bonus issue from the originally planned 2.98 million shares, a Cieszyn official said.
Earlier Polifarb Cieszyn and Wroclaw had said they wanted to carry out the merger to give their shareholders equal control of the new firm.

But last week Pioneer, which has about 10 percent in Cieszyn and 1.5 percent in Wroclaw, said it would seek more control in the new firm for Cieszyn shareholders because it believed Cieszyn was worth more than its Wroclaw namesake.

Wladyslaw Burczak, Polifarb Wroclaw's board member, present at the meeting as an observer, said Monday's decision made the merger unlikely as he believed Wroclaw shareholders would not be willing to accept a change in the original plan when they vote on the plan on Tuesday.
"It is extremely hard to expect a situation where Polifarb Wroclaw shareholders will agree to a change in an earlier accepted merger plan," Burczak said.
"Now we don't know how tomorrow's shareholders' meeting will look like," he added.
The Cieszyn shareholders, who voted not to pay a 1996 dividend, passed a motion that the merger would only be effective if Wroclaw shareholders also skip a 1996 payout.

Cieszyn's shareholders also approved an issue of 22,103,820 shares for Wroclaw shareholders for a one-for-one share exchange to effect the merger on the condition that Wroclaw shareholders accept Cieszyn's no-payout and bonus issue terms.
Bernard Andrzejewski, outgoing Polifarb Cieszyn president, warned the failure of the merger would pitch the two companies against each other scrambling for market share.
"If the merger with Polifarb Wroclaw fails it can turn out that the two companies that wanted to cooperate will fight each other for potential clients," he told the meeting.

Under the plan, first announced last December, the two firms would form a new company, Polifarb Cieszyn-Wroclaw SA, that would command 26 percent market share and account for 40 percent of the domestic paint production.
